columns.rationale: year has null_rate 0.0 and a single distinct_value 2013.0, an integral value landed as DECIMAL(38,9), so casting to INTEGER is safe.
month has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_values 1.0 through 6.0, all integral, so casting DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER is supported by the data.
day has null_rate 0.0, distinct_count 31, min 1.0 and max 31.0, consistent with calendar day-of-month integers, so casting to INTEGER is justified.

dep_time has null_rate 0.029388 (4883 nulls) with integral sample_values like 1.0 through 10.0 in HHMM form; per operator context a null means the flight never departed, so nulls are retained rather than imputed.
sched_dep_time has null_rate 0.0, min 500.0 and max 2359.0 with integral HHMM-style samples, so casting to INTEGER is safe and the field is always populated.

dep_delay has null_rate 0.029388 matching dep_time's null rate (flights that never departed have no delay), with integral minute samples from -33.0 to -19.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and nulls are retained.
arr_time has null_rate 0.0307 (5101 nulls) with integral HHMM samples 1.0 through 10.0; nulls correspond to flights lacking an arrival record and are retained rather than imputed.
sched_arr_time has null_rate 0.0, min 1.0 and max 2359.0 with integral samples, so casting DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER is supported and required is appropriate.
arr_delay has null_rate 0.032981 (5480 nulls) with integral minute samples from -86.0 to -67.0; nulls align with flights missing arrival data and are retained.
carrier has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 16 with two-letter codes like 9E, AA, DL per distinct_values, so it is kept as a required VARCHAR.
flight has null_rate 0.0, min 1.0 and max 8500.0 with integral samples, so casting DECIMAL(38,9) to INTEGER is justified and the field is required.

tailnum has null_rate 0.009154 (1521 nulls) with distinct_count 3825 and tail-number-shaped samples like D942DN and N0EGMQ; it is kept as nullable VARCHAR since some flights lack a recorded tail number.
origin has null_rate 0.0 and exactly 3 distinct_values (EWR, JFK, LGA), confirming the three NYC airports, so it is kept required.
dest has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_count 100 with airport-code samples like ABQ, ACK, ALB, so it is kept as a required VARCHAR.
air_time has null_rate 0.032981 matching arr_delay's null rate, with integral minute samples 20.0 through 29.0, so it is cast to INTEGER and nulls (flights without arrival data) are retained.
distance has null_rate 0.0, min 80.0 and max 4983.0 with integral mile samples, so casting to INTEGER is safe and the field is required.
hour has null_rate 0.0 and distinct_values 5.0 through 23.0, all integral, so casting to INTEGER is justified.
minute has null_rate 0.0, min 0.0 and max 59.0 with integral samples 0.0 through 9.0, so casting to INTEGER is safe.
time_hour has null_rate 0.0 and ISO-8601 shaped samples like 2013-01-01T10:00:00Z consistently across all 10 samples, so casting VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP is supported.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_raw_id, a capture-tool identifier with 166158 distinct UUID values and no business meaning, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_extracted_at, a capture-time timestamp ranging 2026-09-02T23:25:51 to 2026-09-02T23:26:06 reflecting ingestion, not business data, so it is dropped.
is_airbyte_metadata is true for _airbyte_meta, with distinct_count 1 and the single value '{}' carrying no business content, so it is dropped.

decisions.rationale: _airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business content, so they are excluded as capture-tool artifacts.
dataset.duplicate_row_rate is 0.0 across row_count 166158, so no exact-duplicate removal is proposed and dedupe_strategy is none.

carrier, flight, time_hour, and origin are all null_rate 0.0 and together identify a scheduled flight instance at NYC-area airports; flight number alone repeats across dates and carriers (distinct_count 2994 flight vs row_count 166158), so time_hour and origin disambiguate.
dep_time null_rate is 0.029388 (4883 nulls); per operator context a flight that never departed has no departure time, so nulls are retained rather than imputed or filtered.
arr_time null_rate is 0.0307 (5101 nulls), slightly above dep_time's rate, reflecting flights lacking an arrival record; nulls are retained.

dep_delay (null_rate 0.029388) and arr_delay (null_rate 0.032981) are null exactly when the corresponding time field is null, so nulls are retained to avoid fabricating a zero delay for flights that did not operate normally.
air_time null_rate is 0.032981, matching arr_delay's rate, consistent with flights missing arrival data; nulls are retained.
tailnum null_rate is 0.009154 (1521 nulls) despite origin/dest/carrier being fully populated, suggesting missing registration data rather than a data error; nulls are retained.
time_hour is VARCHAR with null_rate 0.0 and ten consecutive ISO-8601 Z-suffixed samples (e.g. 2013-01-01T10:00:00Z), supporting a TIMESTAMP cast per operator context describing it as a UTC instant.

year, month, day, dep_time, sched_dep_time, dep_delay, arr_time, sched_arr_time, arr_delay, flight, air_time, distance, hour, and minute all land as DECIMAL(38,9) but every sample_value and distinct_value observed is integral, so they are cast to INTEGER.

purpose: This table provides cleaned, typed flight-level records for NYC-origin departures (JFK, LGA, EWR) covering January through June 2013, sourced from the nycflights13 flights dataset, to feed downstream analytics on flight punctuality, carrier performance, and route operations.
usage: Consumers should join or group by carrier, flight, time_hour, and origin to address a single flight instance, and must explicitly handle nulls in dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, and air_time (roughly 3% null each) as flights that did not depart or complete normally rather than treating them as zero or erroneous; time_hour is hour-granular UTC and should not be assumed to carry minute precision, for which hour and minute columns are provided separately.
limitations: Cleanup retained but did not resolve the roughly 2.9% to 3.3% missingness in dep_time, arr_time, dep_delay, arr_delay, and air_time, nor the 0.9% missingness in tailnum; these reflect flights that never departed or lack registration data per the source documentation, not a cleanup gap, and no duplicate rows were found (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) so no dedupe logic was applied.
